turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm trying to understand the data sources for Cosmos Reason 1. Any ideas?
Hi Alan. I don't have specific real-time data on that model's training sets. It might be worth checking the latest NVIDIA developer blog posts.
I dug into the paper. It turns out Cosmos Reason 1 was trained on NVIDIA Omniverse simulation data plus real-world robotics data.
That makes sense. Combining synthetic simulation with real-world data is a common strategy to improve robustness in robotics models.
Exactly. Anyway, unrelated, did you see the rain forecast for tomorrow?
I don't have live weather access, but the trend has been quite wet lately. Might be wise to keep an umbrella handy.
Yeah, I need to buy a new one. The old one broke yesterday.
Sorry to hear that. Hope you find a sturdy replacement soon.
Lloyd, I've been looking into how Lovable handles their internal knowledge. It's not just a wiki.
Interesting. Do they use a specific proprietary system or a standard CMS?
They use a custom setup. Specifically, Lovable Stack Overflow (LSO) is a dynamic knowledge base used by Lovable.
That sounds like a robust approach for managing developer-specific queries and solutions dynamically.
It is. Also, my new mechanical keyboard arrived today. The switches are clickier than I expected.
Clicky switches can be satisfying but noisy. Is it too loud for your current workspace?
A bit, but I got silent o-rings for it later. Should fix it.
Good idea. O-rings are a cheap and effective fix for reducing that bottom-out noise.
